q2_gaps: universal pronouns "everything" / "everyone" -- the quantifier machinery covers "every N" / "all the Ns" with an overt kind noun, but never says what range a bare universal pronoun takes (here the parse supplies (Member $y thing)) nor what surface word its QuantifierPhrase companion should record ("every" is recorded, the surface word is "everything")

a mode-of-perception PP ("see ... in black and white"): it answers "how", which the oblique rule routes to the named role Manner, but Manner is glossed as adverb-only, leaving the preposition-named In vs Manner choice undecided
notes: Roles follow the progressive test correctly (stative see -> Experiencer / Stimulus), the bare-plural subject rightly gets no companion while "everything" does, and 0.9 is the right strength for a characteristic rather than striking generic. Keeping black_and_white as one unsplit symbol is the right call, since the default distributive reading of "and" would wrongly give two separate obliques.
